proposal.hypothesis: After translating the stapler 0.02 m along the simulator x-axis while preserving the official task, the policy can satisfy the official goal yet finish with the left TCP farther from the stapler than the right TCP, revealing a bounded spatial asymmetry.

requested_perturbation.description: Translate the stapler from its official baseline position by +0.02 m along the simulator x-axis.
controlled_changes: stapler x-position: official baseline -> baseline +0.02 m

scene_need.description: Construct or adapt the scene by translating the stapler from its official baseline position by +0.02 m along the simulator x-axis.

checker_need.description: Return true only when the official core predicate and the added terminal-state relation both hold: official goal AND terminal Euclidean distance from the left TCP to the stapler is greater than terminal Euclidean distance from the right TCP to the stapler.

rule_tool_need.description: Report one scalar observation: the terminal signed TCP-distance difference, terminal left-TCP-to-stapler distance minus terminal right-TCP-to-stapler distance.

proposal.rationale: The unchanged official control succeeded with an authoritative official_check_success value of 1.0, so baseline task reliability is not the next uncertainty, and no experimental scalar has established a factor boundary. The most informative supported orthogonal concern is a bounded spatial translation of the only tracked task actor, paired with a directly observable terminal comparison between the two TCP-to-stapler distances. The checker tests the boolean weakness witness while the Rule Tool independently reports its scalar magnitude.
